column1: # ComputerBase — AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D vs. 7800X3D, 5800X3D & Core Ultra im Test.
# Gaming-Benchmarks, 720p. 720p is deliberate: a CPU-scaling review removes the
# graphics card as a limit so the processors actually separate.
# THE WHOLE PARCOURS, not one game. The file this replaces took Ghost of
# Tsushima alone from a review that benchmarks 15 games across 47 charts.
# ⚠️ THIS REVIEW SHARES A RENDER SCALE WITH THE RX 9070 GPU REVIEW ON ONLY THREE
# GAMES — ghost-of-tsushima, horizon-forbidden-west and f1-24 — because a CPU
# test reaches for aggressive upsampling ON PURPOSE. Frostpunk 2, Hellblade 2 and
# Space Marine 2 run DLSS Ultra Performance here and native in the GPU review, so
# their cells stay separate and answer nothing rather than blending a third-scale
# render with a native one. That is the upscaling cell key doing its job.
# Settings read per game off "Die Einstellungen der 15 Spiele im Detail" on the
# article's benchmark page. Never inferred, and never carried across from the GPU
# review — same outlet is not the same setting.
# DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED, so every row here shares the one recorded test system:
#   · Ryzen 7 7800X3D — ran DDR5-5200CL30, not the DDR5-5600CL32 standard
#   · Ryzen 7 5800X3D — AM4 on DDR4-3200CL14, a different platform entirely
#   · every Turbo-Mode and DDR5-OC row — non-stock configurations that collide on
#     entry id with their stock counterparts, where the importer's dedupe
#   · Cyberpunk — run with RT Niedrig and no preset named
#   · Homeworld 3 — "DLSS" with no quality stated; the corpus refuses an
#     upscaler whose render fraction nobody wrote down
#   · every CPU Package Power chart — a wattage, not a frame rate
# Intel's "(Perf.)" rows ARE kept: that is the stock power profile, and it is
# what the twelve rows previously committed from this review used.
# RAM capacity/sticks are ComputerBase's standard kit; the article states the
# speed and timing (DDR5-5600CL32) but not the capacity.
